title: AI Joins the Industrial Attack Workflow
content_md: The recent cyberattack on French refrigerators and our tracking of the malicious AI framework ARTEX show that threat actors are increasingly using AI to accelerate attacks, expand their reach, and improve their effectiveness. GreenJuliett, the group behind OT cyberattacks similar to those in France, has begun incorporating AI into its operational technology (OT) attack chain. Understanding the scale AI offers financially motivated and state-sponsored threat actors helps us see it as more than a tool: it’s something that can fill an operator’s role, even while humans remain in control. On October 11 and 12, 2026, someone changed the defrost settings on refrigeration controllers at more than 700 retail locations in France. This resulted in fires, damaged equipment, and food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros, highlighting the physical impacts of attacks against operational technology (OT). On November 9, France attributed the attack to Shahid Kaveh, a unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Cyber Electronic Command (IRGC-CEC).
